method: Compared exact source expression/sentence/meaning and current hold decision with candidate selected owner brief, target pattern and seven-step purpose. A historical medium-confidence label was not treated as authorisation to create a duplicate or awkward lesson.

rows.exactSourceSentence: A freelancer who draws a line around their time can protect evenings for family.
rows.exactSourceExpression: draws a line around their time
rows.sourceMeaning: Sets a firm boundary on when time is available; drawing a line is figurative.
rows.specificReason: Owner 463 explicitly teaches practical time boundaries between work and family commitments; a freelancer protecting evenings makes the same learner decision. The around-their-time syntax would need a bounded owner variant, not a duplicate seven-step lesson.

comparedOwners.meaningEn: Set a boundary that keeps two areas of life or activity from intruding on one another.

rows.exactSourceSentence: The editor chose to cut away the long introduction.
rows.sourceMeaning: Remove an unnecessary section during editing; a useful phrasal verb.
rows.specificReason: The exact guide uses cut away the long introduction for deletion. That object is more naturally cut or cut out; cut away also has a separate camera/scene-shift use. A target broad enough to cover the source would conflate senses; no stable source-faithful seven-step unit established.

rows.exactSourceSentence: The story can speak different emotional languages to children and parents.
rows.sourceMeaning: Connect with different groups through different feelings; language is figurative.
rows.specificReason: The story speaking different emotional languages to children and parents is a crafted audience-response metaphor. Owner 1577 instead teaches people understanding each other by speaking the same emotional language. The source is distinct from that owner, but a fixed transferable target and six varied assessed decisions have not been substantiated.

comparedOwners.meaningEn: Understand and respond to one another’s feelings in a familiar, compatible way.

rows.exactSourceSentence: Parents should not let a device run the child's day.
rows.sourceMeaning: Control a child's routine; running is figurative.
rows.specificReason: Owner 2458 teaches an app or schedule dictating a person’s daily choices rather than assisting. Letting a device run the child’s day is the same agency/control decision with a narrower day object; assess a bounded owner variant, not a duplicate lesson.

comparedOwners.meaningEn: Control a person’s daily choices or routine instead of merely assisting them.

rows.exactSourceSentence: The community worked to stitch it back together.
rows.sourceMeaning: Restore something that was fragmented; a fabric metaphor.
rows.specificReason: Owner 1357 already teaches repairing a fractured community by knitting its social fabric back together; selected owner 3823 separately teaches the network noun. Stitch it back together refers only to it, with no named antecedent in the exact source, so a separate lesson risks duplicating restoration and inventing its object.

comparedOwners.titleEn: knit the social fabric back together
comparedOwners.meaningEn: Help restore the relationships and cooperation that connect a community after strain or division.
The network of relationships and cooperation that connects members of a community or society.

rows.exactSourceSentence: A small dinner can mark a moment beautifully.
rows.sourceMeaning: Recognise an occasion as significant; a natural celebratory collocation.
rows.specificReason: Owner 1468 already teaches recognising or commemorating a meaningful event with a small gathering; the source small dinner marking a moment requires the same decision. Mark a moment is transparent wording and does not justify a new seven-step owner.

comparedOwners.meaningEn: Recognise or commemorate an event, achievement or moment that matters.
